input.question: "The power to tax is the power to destroy." -Chief Justice John Marshall
input.ground_truth: Taxation can very easily be used to cause people to take some action, or to discourage another. We want people to buy solar panels or health insurance, so we provide tax credits to those that buy the things we want. We don't want people to buy tobacco, so we put high taxes on it. If those taxes were ever set high enough, it could literally shut down the legal tobacco industry. That's the power to destroy an industry through taxation.

Wearing a suit and tie makes me feel confident. What do you think?

That’s a great feeling! Wearing a suit and tie can definitely boost confidence for many people. There’s something about dressing up that can make you feel put-together, professional, and ready to take on the day. Clothes can have a powerful psychological effect—sometimes just changing what you wear can change how you see yourself and how others perceive you. If it makes you feel good and confident, that’s what matters most. Do you wear a suit and tie for special occasions, work, or just for the feeling it gives you?

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: "The power to tax is the power to destroy." -Chief Justice John Marshall

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy box with all your favorite toys. Now, imagine your grown-up says, “Every time you play with a toy, you have to give me some of your candy.” If you have to give away all your candy, you won’t have any left to enjoy. The grown-up can decide how much candy you give, and if they ask for too much, you won’t have any candy at all.

That’s what Chief Justice John Marshall meant. When the government can make you pay taxes, they decide how much you have to give them. If they ask for too much, it can make it hard for you to have money for things you need. So, having the power to make people pay taxes is a very important and powerful thing—it can help or hurt people.
